spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the product argument for accuracyMode:'approximate' with a real ranking pipeline — haversine distances over a fixed branch list, a grid-snap coarsening that mirrors what a coarse fix is, and an honest comparison against the exact ranking — plus a live path that requests an approximate fix.

interactive.rationale: Origin select, a stepped coarsening slider with datalist labels, live-location and reset buttons all re-rank the table live; the initial render was observed running at load.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises a working nearest-branch finder where the coarse fix usually picks the same branch — exactly what the page computes and says, including the failure direction when coarsening beats branch spacing.

edge_cases.rationale: The verdict logic covers the case where coarsening genuinely changes the nearest branch (and says the use case then needs precise), the live-fix error branches fall back to preset origins with explanatory copy, and the true ranking is always computed from the exact origin so the coarse answer can be honestly graded.

conformance.rationale: Relies on the feature-level suite, which proves the getter-read, enum negative and default contracts; on Chromium 141 the route ran 6 pass / 2 fail — the correct pre-157 split.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): initial render observed live (console 'coarsen=0m nearestSame=true shifted=0', 'ready with 10 branches') with the ranked table populated in both screenshots; slider, origin switch and live-location paths are click-driven and judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires 'ranking-compared' on every render including the observed initial one, plus live-origin success/failure; console is clean.

design_system.rationale: Variables and button overrides are correct, but the emerald 'yes' agreement cells (--accent-emerald #0a8f5c on --bg-paper white, ~4.1:1) sit below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for their 0.9rem bold text; the rose 'no' state passes.

accessibility.rationale: The verdict is an aria-live=polite output, the table has a caption and column headers, the coarsening slider is labelled with a live value and datalist tick labels, and agreement is conveyed by text ('yes' / 'no — truly #N'), not colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At a true 360px viewport the five-column ranking table forces the stage past the viewport and the body's overflow clip cuts off the amber note text and the 'Same answer?' column (visible in the mobile capture); desktop at 1280px is clean.

openQuestions.title: Ranking table overflows and clips the stage at mobile width
openQuestions.detail: Same failure family as the sibling accuracy-mode-probe page: the table's min-content width exceeds 360px, the grid stage stretches to fit it, and body overflow-x:hidden crops the note and the last table column ('Same answer?' shows as 'Sam ans'). Give the table its own overflow-x:auto wrapper or restack columns at narrow widths, and re-verify at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Caption renders 'the exact origin origin'
openQuestions.detail: The caption template ends with a literal 'origin' after the #origin-desc span, and render() writes 'exact origin' / 'origin coarsened to N' into the span, producing 'Branches ranked from the exact origin origin' (visible in the desktop capture). Drop the trailing word from the template or the leading/trailing 'origin' from the injected strings.

openQuestions.title: Emerald 'yes' cells miss WCAG AA on white
openQuestions.detail: --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-paper is ~4.1:1, below 4.5:1 at 0.9rem bold. Part of the recurring shared-palette shortfall recorded across this pass; one palette-level fix would clear all instances.

summary: The best kind of use-case demo: a real ranking pipeline whose coarsening is computed rather than narrated, always graded against the exact ranking so the page can honestly report when approximate would give the wrong branch. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/approximate-geolocation/store-locator/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots with the initial exact ranking rendered — Southwark Bridge first with five agreeing rows — clean console, feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). Slider and live-location interactions judged from wiring. Two visible defects: the ranking table clips the stage at 360px (parity fail), and the caption doubles the word 'origin'.
